summary: PARTIAL is right, but one piece of the auditor's evidence is wrong. The finding said the root `effect` and `@ryco/contracts` barrels sit in the mobile startup graph and tree shaking is off. Fixed: the root barrels are gone. There are 0 non-test value imports, down from 3/24/64/14 files in mobile/client-runtime/contracts/shared. A lint rule guards both roots, and e8b023912 measured 2993 -> 2981 bundle modules. Still open: Expo tree shaking is unset, and the `effect/rpc` and `effect/reactivity` sub-barrels remain. I reproduced the auditor's estimate that switching both to deep imports drops 47 effect modules (about 406 KiB raw, about 300 KB once JSDoc is stripped). The auditor was wrong that contracts `rpc.ts` is out of the launch graph. A walker that copies mobileStartupImports.test.ts finds this chain: index.ts -> src/state/threadsRuntime.ts -> client-runtime state/threads/index.ts -> threadFork.ts -> rpc/protocol.ts -> contracts/rpc.ts. Chat forking (#708) added it after the report. Launch-reachable contracts are 56 modules / 890 KiB, not 51 / 707 KiB. Even without that chain, rpc.ts runs when the first environment connects (environmentDriver.ts:333 builds the WsTransport). That pulls in 48 contracts modules / 736 KiB, so lazy schema construction is still a valid low-priority idea, not a moot one.

evidence.note: EFFECT_ROOT_IMPORT and CONTRACTS_ROOT_IMPORT (line 19, allowTypeImports) are no-restricted-imports paths. They apply to client-runtime src (125), contracts/shared src (137) and apps/mobile (167). Neither `effect/rpc` nor `effect/reactivity` is restricted.

Now `import * as Schema from "effect/Schema"`. `git grep 'from "effect";'` finds 0 non-test hits in mobile, client-runtime, contracts and shared. The only remaining hit is packages/client-runtime/test/fakeWebSocket.ts:1, a test helper. Codemod landed in 60633eff3 (#710).

One of 5 inline-type-only `import { type X } from "@ryco/contracts"` declarations. babel-preset-expo runs @babel/plugin-transform-typescript with onlyRemoveTypeImports=false (default), so isAllSpecifiersElided removes the whole declaration. No side-effect import of the root is left, so no defect. I found no value imports of either root.
`import { RpcClient, RpcSerialization } from "effect/rpc"` loads dist/rpc/index.js, which re-exports RpcServer, RpcTest, RpcWorker and others with `export * as`. wsTransport.ts:10 does the same.

10 non-test files import the `effect/reactivity` index (atomRegistry.ts:1, invalidation.ts:6, keyedQuery.ts:2, requestLatencyState.ts:1, serverState.ts:12, wsConnectionState.ts:2, sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts:2, mobile checkpointDiffAtoms.ts:14, mobile useNewTaskRepository.ts:2). That index re-exports AtomHttpApi -> http-api/HttpApiClient and the http server stack. Closure over effect@4.0.2 dist: 235 modules / 4,460 KiB now, 188 / 4,054 KiB with deep imports, 47 fewer. Deep-importing only rpc saves 7 and only reactivity saves 13; most of the saving needs both, because RpcServer/http server and AtomHttpApi/http-api share most of the dropped modules. @effect/atom-react already uses deep reactivity imports; its only barrel reference is in JSDoc.

Value import of isAwaitingAdmission / RpcRequestRefusedError from ../../rpc/protocol.ts. state/threads/index.ts:11 has `export * from "./threadFork.ts"`, and apps/mobile/index.ts imports src/state/threadsRuntime bare. So contracts/rpc.ts and the effect/rpc barrel are in the static launch graph, contrary to the auditor. Added by 1cc2ab13b (#708, chat forking), after the report. With inline requires the protocol import is deferred to first use, at line 593 inside a function.

Every saved environment connection runs createWsRpcClient(new WsTransport(...)), which evaluates protocol.ts -> @ryco/contracts/rpc (rpc closure: 48 of 70 contracts modules, 736 KiB) and the effect/rpc barrel. On a paired device this happens right after launch, inline requires or not.

experimentalImportSupport plus inlineRequires (1b8bfd183). That commit states the bundle keeps the same 3,017 source modules. A barrel's `export * as` re-exports are top-level references, so evaluating a barrel still evaluates every re-exported module. No EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH or EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING appears anywhere in the repo or in apps/mobile/eas.json build env. @expo/cli metroOptions.js:78-84 still gates tree shaking on both. EAS dashboard env for `environment: production` cannot be checked from the repo.

The startup guard test collapses every `effect/...` specifier to `pkg:effect` (resolveSpecifier), so it cannot detect sub-barrels or the root. It never asserts that packages/contracts/src/index.ts is unreachable, so the lint rule is the only guard. Its header still says 'no inline requires', which has been stale since 1b8bfd183.

remaining: 1. Effect sub-barrels: packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:8 and wsTransport.ts:10 import the `effect/rpc` index. About 10 non-test files import the `effect/reactivity` index: client-runtime connection/atomRpcClient.ts:3, rpc/atomRegistry.ts:1, rpc/invalidation.ts:6, rpc/keyedQuery.ts:2, rpc/requestLatencyState.ts:1, rpc/serverState.ts:12, rpc/wsConnectionState.ts:2, sourceControlDiscoveryState.ts:2, and mobile src/rpc/checkpointDiffAtoms.ts:14 and src/features/newTask/useNewTaskRepository.ts:2. Together they add 47 effect modules (about 406 KiB raw, about 300 KB without JSDoc: RpcServer, RpcTest, the http server/router/multipart stack, http-api client, AtomHttpApi and others) to the bundle. Those modules evaluate when the reactivity index is first touched (module-scope Atom.make in launch state modules) and at first RPC connection. vite.config.ts does not restrict either sub-barrel. 2. Proposal part 3, the Expo tree-shaking release-build experiment (EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH=1 + EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING=1), was never run. Tree shaking would also prune the sub-barrels above, since effect is ESM with sideEffects limited to the JIT enable file. 3. Proposal part 2b, lazy construction of rarely used RPC families, was never done. It is not moot: contracts/rpc.ts is statically reachable at launch through threadFork.ts:25 and is evaluated at the first environment connection. It builds the whole group over 48 contracts modules / 736 KiB at module scope, with the largest being orchestration.ts 137 KiB and agentControl.ts 106 KiB.
fixDefects: No functional defects in the implemented fixes. The lint rules correctly allow type-only imports of the contracts root: inline `type` specifiers are fully elided by babel-preset-expo (onlyRemoveTypeImports=false), so no side-effect import survives. The startup guard test has two gaps. It cannot see effect barrels because resolveSpecifier collapses `effect/...` to `pkg:effect`, and it does not assert that packages/contracts/src/index.ts is unreachable, so only the lint rule protects against a regression. Its header comment ('no inline requires') is stale since 1b8bfd183. The auditor's measurement that rpc.ts is out of the launch graph was wrong; the threadFork.ts:25 chain added by #708 puts it back in.
implementationSketch: A. Effect sub-barrel codemod (S, low risk). In packages/client-runtime/src/rpc/protocol.ts:8, replace the import with `import * as RpcClient from "effect/rpc/RpcClient"` and `import * as RpcSerialization from "effect/rpc/RpcSerialization"`. Do the same in wsTransport.ts:10. In each reactivity importer, use `import * as Atom from "effect/reactivity/Atom"`, `import * as AtomRegistry from "effect/reactivity/AtomRegistry"`, `import * as AtomRpc from "effect/reactivity/AtomRpc"` and `import * as Reactivity from "effect/reactivity/Reactivity"`. Type-only uses such as `type AtomRegistry` become `import type * as AtomRegistry from ...`. effect's exports map `./*` -> `./dist/*.js` already resolves these subpaths. In vite.config.ts, add EFFECT_SUBBARREL_IMPORTS (names: effect/rpc, effect/reactivity, effect/http, effect/http-api, effect/socket, effect/schema, effect/encoding and the other `./<dir>` index entries of effect's package.json) to the same `paths` arrays as EFFECT_ROOT_IMPORT at lines 125, 137, 167 and 188. oxlint matches `paths` names exactly, so deep subpaths stay allowed. In apps/mobile/src/perf/mobileStartupImports.test.ts, make resolveSpecifier keep the full `effect/...` specifier (e.g. `pkg:effect/rpc`) instead of collapsing to `pkg:effect`. Then add a test asserting staticGraph('index.ts') contains no `pkg:effect`, no `pkg:effect/<barrel-dir>` and no packages/contracts/src/index.ts. Fix the stale 'no inline requires' header. Verify with focused checks: vitest on that test file and oxlint on the touched files. In a scratch worktree outside the repo, compare `npx expo export --platform ios` module count and Hermes bytecode size before and after; expect about 47 fewer modules. B. Tree-shaking trial (M, experiment only). In a scratch worktree, build an iOS release export with EXPO_UNSTABLE_METRO_OPTIMIZE_GRAPH=1 EXPO_UNSTABLE_TREE_SHAKING=1. Compare bundle modules and bytecode size, plus the 1b8bfd183 launch harness (modules evaluated by splash hide, bundle start -> first App commit, splash hide), over 2x10 alternating release-simulator launches. Check that the metro.config.js resolver override forcing isESMImport for @ryco/* and CJS-resolved packages (tabler) still behave, and that the threadsRuntime/hostedHub bare-import registrations survive. Adopt only if the gain is measurable, by setting the env in apps/mobile/eas.json build.{preview,production}.env. C. Optional (M, medium risk). Defer construction of rarely used RPC families in packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts, for example agentControl, atlassian, automationCentre, cliProxy, codexResetCredits, changeRequestReview, acpRegistry and sessionImport payloads, using Schema.suspend. Alternatively, give mobile a narrower RpcGroup with only the methods it calls. Measure Hermes time from WsTransport creation to first request before doing it. Contracts round-trip tests must confirm encoding is unchanged.
decisionReason: These are build and import-path changes only. No auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle, Hub protocol or product behaviour is affected. Shipping tree shaking would need normal release QA, not a product decision.
